newsitem.title: UK: Copper in long term bear market - consultant.
newsitem.headline: Copper in long term bear market - consultant.

text.p: Copper has now entered a long term bear market, said mining and metal industry consultants Brook Hunt in its latest study of mine costs.

The report acknowledged prospects for further significant gains in world-wide demand but expressed concern about the rapid increase in mine production and the fact that the industry's cost structure remains extremely robust even at the less elevated copper prices seen in recent months.

Despite the sharp fall in copper prices, which will result in the 1996 London Metal Exchange average being over 20 percent down on the previous year, copper miners' average cash margins in 1996 were again high at around 40 percent, Brook Hunt said.

The report estimated that by the year 2000 more than a third of mine capacity in operation at that time will have been commissioned since 1990 and avergae direct costs at those new mines will be 15 percent lower than the average for producers already in existence prior to 1990.
